text:
clare: quick flag - sekai-v1 int4 bring-up showing locale-specific detok corruption. ran multilingual-eval-suite and saw ZWJ/ZWSP disappear in mixed CJK+emoji, plus mirrored parens in RTL runs. full eval: https://rwd.internal/evals/1780000000 :warning:

clare: summary numbers: zh chrF -3.7, ja BLEU -1.5, he/parens mirror +11%, emoji ZWJ drop 4.6%.

bo: can you paste a tiny repro (fp16 vs int4) and tokenizer preview? wondering if this is a pruning/quant packing corner-case that strips zero-widths.

clare: repros below (literal unicode shown):
```
src: \u6211\u559c\u6b22\u4f5c\u8a00\ud83d\ude0a\u200d\u2642\ufe0f\u3002
fp16: I like writing.\ud83d\ude0a\u200d\u2642\ufe0f
int4: I like writing. \ud83d\ude0a\ufe0f  <-- ZWJ (\u200d) dropped, skin/sex-variant collapsed
```
```
src: (\u05e9\u05dc\u05d9\u05dd) \u05d1\u05e8\u05d0\u05d4
fp16: (Shl\u00e9m) Brave
int4: ) Shl\u00e9m ) Brave  <-- paren mirrored and duplicated
```

ying: tokenizer peek: `tokenize('\u6211\u559c\u6b22\u4f5c\u8a00\ud83d\ude0a\u200d\u2642\ufe0f\u3002') -> ['\u6211','\u559c\u6b22','\u4f5c','\u8a00', '\ud83d\ude0a\u200d\u2642\ufe0f','\u3002']` but post-quant embedding-id for the zwj-emoji whole token collapsed to same id as simple emoji and the ZWJ byte sequence absent in serialized vocab.

omar: immediate sanity run: `rwd evaluate --model sekai-v1 --quant=int4 --no-token-prune --dataset multilingual-eval-suite`

clare: ran it. result improved: zh chrF -1.0, ja BLEU -0.3, he paren mirror drop to +1.4%, emoji ZWJ preserved. so token-prune step is the likely suspect.

build-bot: build: sekai-v1-int4 image built (sha256:ffeeaabb... ) :package: 1780000300

bo: two quick hypotheses: 1) token-prune merges low-frequency multi-codepoint tokens into nearest ascii-like token id (bad token collision), 2) serialization step strips zero-width codepoints to save bytes leading to different detok behavior.

ying: looked at `vocab_before` vs `vocab_after` for the emoji token: `vocab_before['\ud83d\ude0a\u200d\u2642\ufe0f'] = id_9021`, `vocab_after['\ud83d\ude0a\u200d\u2642\ufe0f'] = null` and the simple emoji `\ud83d\ude0a` now maps to id_9021. so prune removed the zwj-joined token and re-pointed the id to the base emoji. that explains the semantic collapse.

omar: created ML-2705 "sekai-v1: token-prune removes ZWJ/ZWSP tokens during int4 pipeline causing locale detok regressions" assigned to @ying + @omar. https://rwd.internal/issue/ML-2705

clare: added failing promptset to ticket and a micro-bisect: `./scripts/bisect_token_prune.sh --model sekai-v1 --quant=int4 --steps 16`.

bo: immediate mitigation: disable aggressive token-prune for builds that include multi-codepoint emoji and preserve zero-width joiner tokens. also add a unit test that asserts any token containing ZWJ (\u200d) or ZWSP (\u200b) is preserved during prune.

ying: patch underway 1: adding a safety whitelist for codepoints in U+2000..U+200F and emoji zwj sequences and making prune use stable ordering by token codepoint sequence rather than hash.

omar: plan: add token-diff output to eval UI that highlights removed/merged multi-codepoint tokens and flag builds where any ZWJ/ZWSP token id changes. add canary job to quant pipeline to run that check.

clare: cool. if anyone spots other mixed-orient/emoji corruption ping here. thanks :pray:
